data.why: The dashboard's Collect Data > Upload tab accepts any CSV and auto-detects columns; the repo's own CAMELS daily-discharge CSV (date, discharge_cms, precipitation_mm) exercises flood-frequency/hydrology analyses, and a small synthetic long-format water-quality CSV (sample_datetime, station_id, parameter, value, discharge, lat/lon, with a missing value and a turbidity outlier) exercises the EDA/quality-alerts workflow the same way the built-in demo dataset does.

goals: Load a gauge's discharge record and run flood-frequency analysis (GEV/LP3/Gumbel) to get design flows and return periods
Upload a water-quality dataset, run the automated EDA and quality assessment, and spot outliers or data gaps
Visualize a hydrograph and the inferred columns of an uploaded dataset with interactive Plotly charts
Run baseflow separation and hydrological signatures on a long daily-discharge series
Ask the AI methodology recommender for a suggested analysis given a dataset profile and research goal
Export analysis results and figures from the workspace dataset

review.summary: The tree accurately covers the dashboard's intake, quality, visualization, streamflow and flood-frequency workflow, its evidence checks out, and the labels are well split between general and specific. Before filing it needs the AI recommender, FAO-56 and groundwater stages, a corrected ordering of screening and cleaning, a cleaned-up flood-frequency task, and a re-cut of the generic analysis-selector feature.
